questions.prompt: The coefficient of \(x^{2}\) in the expansion of \((1+3x)^{-\frac{1}{2}}\) is ______
The remainder when \(3^{268}\) is divided by \(26\) is ______
questions.explanation: \(3^{3}=27=26\times1+1\). Write \(268=3\times89+1\), so \(3^{268}=(26+1)^{89}\cdot3^{1}\). By the binomial theorem every term of the bracket except the last is a multiple of \(26\), so the remainder comes from \(1\cdot3^{1}\) = \(3\), which leaves remainder \(3\).

questions.prompt: In Pascal's triangle the entry below the neighbours \(3003\) and \(2002\) is ______
The greatest integer dividing \(n(n+1)(2n+1)\) for all positive integers \(n\) is ______

questions.prompt: The unit digit of \(38^{604}\) is ______
questions.explanation: The last digit of \(38\) is \(8\); its powers end in \(8,4,2,6\) and repeat (cyclicity \(4\)). \(604=4\times151+0\), so take place \(4\): last digit \(6\).

questions.prompt: The unit digit of \(12^{446}\) is ______
questions.explanation: The last digit of \(12\) is \(2\); its powers end in \(2,4,8,6\) and repeat (cyclicity \(4\)). \(446=4\times111+2\), so take place \(2\): last digit \(4\).

questions.prompt: The remainder when \(9^{215}\) is divided by \(20\) is ______
questions.explanation: \(9^{2}=81=20\times4+1\). Write \(215=2\times107+1\), so \(9^{215}=(80+1)^{107}\cdot9^{1}\). By the binomial theorem every term of the bracket except the last is a multiple of \(20\), so the remainder comes from \(1\cdot9^{1}\) = \(9\), which leaves remainder \(9\).

questions.prompt: The unit digit of \(82^{267}\) is ______

questions.prompt: The smallest positive integer \(n_{0}\) for which \(5^{n}>2^{n}+4\) for all \(n\ge n_{0}\) is ______
questions.explanation: At \(n=1\) the values are \(5\) and \(6\), so the inequality fails; at \(n=2\) we get \(25>8\), and the inductive step then keeps it true for every larger \(n\). So the basis step starts at \(n=2\).

questions.prompt: The sum of the coefficients at the even places of \((1+x)^{13}\) is ______
questions.explanation: Even-place sum = odd-place sum, and together they make \(2^{13}\), so each is \(2^{12}=4096\).
